correctness.rationale: The order on B2 has four labelled worlds, 12 free off-diagonal relation bits. I independently enumerated all 4096 reflexive relations, checked transitivity by R(y)⊆R(x) for each xRy and applied the exact fully quantified Fischer–Servi F1/F2 tests to every x,y,z with order cones {all},{middle,top},{middle,top},{top}. The accepted set contains 135 relations; endpoint patterns (0R1,1R0) have counts 76,29,29,1. Swapping the two incomparable middle worlds preserves the set and fixes 27 relations, giving 81 orbits by Burnside. Direct argument shows both endpoint edges force complete R using F1 and F2 and transitivity. Read the package's independent alternative generator via partitions and antisymmetric quotient orders (355 preorders) and its exact set comparison. This is an exhaustive finite certificate for exactly four worlds, not extrapolation to larger lattices.

value.rationale: The Boolean diamond is the first finite lattice with incomparable intermediate worlds and a common join, beyond the chain and rooted-fork cases. Its complete admissible IS4 birelation census, orbit classes and boundary edge strata provide a natural exact benchmark for constructing and testing finite intuitionistic modal frames. It is a motivated complete small-object classification, not an arbitrarily sliced table.
